assets: the tower/gate verdict on a commit, the only proof the merge queue takes
the gate's rules, scripts and workflows
boundaries: a pull request's code (a session's, or a fork's) and the GitHub-hosted runner that judges it
the pull request run and the merge queue run that reuses its tests' verdict
the staged workflows of this tree and the ones the owner installs in .github/workflows

threats.statement: A run that did not judge the commit, such as a fork's run or a run of another head, passes its green verdict off as the queue commit's; or a tower/gate status is posted on a commit by a credential other than the gate's own job. The ruleset binds each required check to the GitHub Actions app (integration 15368), so a status of that name from a session's credential (verify-commit without --no-post) or any other writer does not count. Residual: the binding is staged in .github/rulesets/main.json and holds once the owner applies it to the live ruleset (VULN-gate-check-source stays open until then).

A pull request edits the gate itself (its scripts, its rules, its registry keys, the verifier or a workflow) so that its own change passes. The gate's files (GATE_FILE: the stages, the structure and commit checks, config/registry/gate/, scripts/verify-commit) ask a decision, and the pinned job of tower/gate judges a change to them with the base's gate: the base's gate_pin.py puts the base's gate files back in the checkout and the plan's stages run there (D-070 on GitHub). Residual: the pinned job is staged in services/runner/github/tower-gate.yml and holds once the owner installs it (VULN-gate-judged-by-own-head stays open until then); the workflow itself is the owner's to change (D-087), and the head's tests run the head's code, as code under test.

A dependency or tool the gate runs is swapped for a malicious version between two runs. Residual: the workflow's actions are pinned by a tag, not a commit; the supply measure counts them unpinned and no check refuses one.
A pushed history is rewritten so that what merged is not what was judged.
A merge cannot be traced to the verdict and the commit that justified it.

A secret committed in a change reaches the public repository and its history. Residual: the gate sees a pushed commit, already public on its branch; the earlier barrier is the pre-push scan, which runs on the client and is skipped by a push that bypasses the hook.

A change floods the queue or hangs the gate, so no other change lands. Residual: the 60 s requirement is a target, not a bound; a hung run is stopped by the job's timeout and the queue's check timeout.

The ruleset requires no approving review (D-055), so any account that may push a branch and enqueue it lands whatever passes the gate's checks; the checks, not a person, are the whole barrier. Residual: a change that is malicious but passes every rule is not caught.

findings.finding: The binding of tower/gate and web to the GitHub Actions app (integration_id 15368) is real in .github/rulesets/main.json and security.test.sh refuses a required check without it, but it is staged: until the owner applies it to the live ruleset a status of that name from any writer counts. The earlier review's 'fixed' was premature while VULN-gate-check-source is open.
findings.reason: needs the owner to apply the staged ruleset; the threat's own residual already says so.

findings.finding: Missing threat: the Actions-app binding does not say which workflow produced the check. A pull_request or merge_group run uses the workflow file of the commit under judgment, so a change that edits .github/workflows/tower-gate.yml (or adds a job named tower/gate to web.yml, an allowed file) gets a green tower/gate from the Actions app by its own definition. gate_workflows.refused only refuses files gate.allowed_workflows does not name, and it runs inside the workflow the change replaced; the .claude/settings.json deny and a token without the workflow scope are client-side, not repository rules.
findings.reason: needs a repository-side barrier for .github/workflows (for example a ruleset path restriction or required review on that path, or a required workflow run from a protected ref); not in place.

findings.finding: The pinned job (services/runner/github/tower-gate.yml) and the overlay (gate_pin.overlay, verify-commit --stages-only) exist and tower/gate needs the job green, but they are staged, not installed (VULN-gate-judged-by-own-head open). The earlier 'fixed' was premature.
findings.reason: needs the owner to install the staged workflow once the overlay is on main.

findings.finding: Even installed, the overlay as written leaves the head in control: (a) GATE_FILE pins only the entry scripts, not the modules they import (config.py, forge_pr.py, plan_tick.py, decision_wait.py, regime.py, unit_check.py, threshold_check.py and the other structure.py imports), so a change to one of them is not a gate change: the pinned job ends after the overlay and gate_errors asks no decision; (b) in the pinned job the head's scripts/cloud/setup.sh and env.sh run after the overlay in the same checkout, and scripts/verify-commit runs the .toolchain/bin/python3 that setup.sh installs, so head code can undo the overlay; (c) the pinned job runs stages only, while the parts run the head's verify_commit, which chooses and runs the tests and records the verdict the merge queue reuses, so a change to the verifier decides its own tests.
findings.reason: needs a change to gate_pin.GATE_FILE (or pinning scripts/lib as a whole) and to the pinned job (toolchain from the base, tests planned by the base); not in place.

findings.finding: Missing threat: config/registry/regime/regime.exception_active.json is true and regime.exception_kept is [money, people], so regime.lifted('structure') and lifted('commit-plan') are true on every tower/gate run (nothing pins the regime outside the script tests' hermetic hook): structure.py under_regime turns every structure-check refusal into a warning, and gate_discipline.lift does the same to the plan, fix-up, one-commit-per-push, plan-completeness and lane refusals. So STD-gate-structure-check refuses nothing today, and the regime keys are outside GATE_FILE, so a change can turn the regime on or empty its kept list with no decision and no pinning.
findings.reason: needs the regime ended or the gate locks kept, and config/registry/regime/ added to the gate files; not in place.

findings.finding: Supply chain: the installed workflow pins actions by tag; the staged one pins the part job's actions by commit but the pinned job still uses actions/checkout@v4 and actions/cache@v4. No check refuses a tag pin, as the residual says.
findings.reason: the residual is honest; the actions are GitHub's own, the party that already runs the runner and the ruleset. The staged pinned job should use the same commit pins as the part job.

findings.finding: History rewrite: the ruleset's non_fast_forward and deletion rules and the merge queue (merge commits only) refuse it on main, and force_push_errors is not lifted by the regime.
The merge commit and the Actions check run trace the verdict; the verdict artifacts expire in 7 days and run logs on GitHub's retention, so the evidence of a reused verdict does not outlive them.
findings.reason: the merge commit and the required check on it are the record; the logs are supporting evidence.

findings.finding: The residual (the gate sees a commit already public; the pre-push scan is client-side and skippable) is honest; the secret stages' output is kept out of the public job log (verify_commit).
findings.reason: holds as stated; the earlier disposition stands.

findings.finding: Job timeout-minutes 30 and the queue's check_response_timeout_minutes 20 bound a hung run; concurrency cancels a superseded run of the same pull request.
The residual is honest, but with the regime lifting the structure and commit-plan locks and the overlay gaps above, the checks are a weaker barrier than the statement says.
findings.reason: kept as written; it holds once the open tampering and spoofing findings are fixed.
